internalLinks.text: Maintenance and oil servicing The model, year, mileage and service history determine the due maintenance items. Oil, filters, fluids and any supported service reset are confirmed from vehicle-specific information before quotation. Rolls-Royce oil service in Dubai

Diagnostics and warning lights Warning messages, misfires, starting concerns and changes in drivability are assessed with compatible fault data and appropriate physical testing. A stored code is evidence, not proof that a part has failed. Rolls-Royce diagnostics in Dubai

Engine, cooling and mechanical concerns Oil leaks, coolant loss, overheating, unusual noise and other mechanical concerns are inspected before a repair route, parts or timing are proposed. Rolls-Royce mechanical repair assessment

Transmission and gearbox assessment Gearbox warnings, leaks, delayed engagement and shift-quality concerns are assessed against the fitted transmission. Fluid, service functions and repair availability are confirmed for the exact vehicle. Rolls-Royce transmission assessment

Air suspension and ride quality Ride-height warnings, leaning, compressor operation, noise and changes in ride quality require identification of the fitted suspension. Parts and supported calibration functions are confirmed before work. Rolls-Royce suspension assessment
Brakes, steering and tyres Brake warnings, vibration, pad and disc condition, steering concerns and tyre wear are measured before parts or alignment work are recommended. Rolls-Royce brake inspection

Electrical and battery concerns Battery drain, low-voltage warnings, no-start concerns and electrical faults are traced with appropriate testing. Coding or programming is not assumed and requires separate confirmation. Rolls-Royce electrical assessment

Air conditioning and cabin climate Weak cooling, airflow, leaks, compressor noise and cabin-zone concerns are tested before refrigerant or parts are proposed. The vehicle label determines the correct refrigerant and service equipment. Rolls-Royce AC assessment

Low-voltage battery and starting concerns Starting, charging and battery-drain concerns are assessed as low-voltage work. Hybrid traction-battery service is not implied and requires separate capability confirmation. Lamborghini battery assessment

Electrical assessment Voltage, wiring, sensors and module communication may require testing. Coding or programming is offered only when access and workshop capability are confirmed. Lamborghini electrical assessment

AC and climate concerns Weak cooling, leaks, airflow and compressor concerns are tested before refrigerant or parts are recommended; the vehicle label determines the specification. Lamborghini AC assessment

No power, no crank or the engine will not start A Mercedes no-start can involve the 12-volt supply, starter circuit, key authorisation, fuel, ignition, engine-speed input or another control fault. The first step is to identify whether the car has no power, will not crank or cranks without starting. Read the Mercedes no-start guide

Suspension Fault or one side sitting low On a Mercedes fitted with AIRMATIC, a low corner or warning can involve an air spring, compressor, valve block, leak, sensor or electrical fault. Confirm the fitted system before testing; ABC and E-ACTIVE BODY CONTROL use different procedures. Understand the AIRMATIC warning

Jerking, slipping or delayed gear engagement 7G-Tronic, 9G-Tronic and AMG SpeedShift symptoms may relate to fluid condition, adaptations, sensors, a conductor plate, mechatronics or internal wear. A scan and road test help define the repair scope. Read the gearbox symptom guide

Engine light, rough idle or loss of power The cause can sit in ignition, air metering, boost, fuel delivery, emissions or cooling—not just the component named by a stored code. XENTRY data and physical testing are used together. Read the check-engine guide

Weak AC, warm air or uneven cabin cooling Poor cabin cooling needs airflow, refrigerant-pressure, leak and climate-control checks. A recharge is appropriate only after the cause and correct refrigerant specification are established. Read the weak-AC guide

Overheating or repeated coolant loss A rising temperature warning concerns engine cooling. Stop safely if overheating is indicated, allow the system to cool and arrange assessment; do not open a hot coolant cap or keep driving to test the warning. Read the engine-overheating guide

Battery warning or intermittent electrical faults A weak main or auxiliary battery, charging fault, voltage drop, wiring concern or control-module communication issue can create several warning messages at once. Any required battery registration or coding is confirmed for compatibility and quoted where supported. Read the battery-warning guide

Brake warning, vibration or reduced confidence Mercedes and AMG brake checks cover pad and disc condition, sensors, calipers, fluid, hydraulic operation and the cause of vibration. The correct parts route depends on the fitted brake package. Mercedes brake repair
